def check_mission3_chair_break_cutscene():
    """Drives the Mission 3 chair-break cutscene end-to-end and asserts the
    in-cell state mutations fire at the Crack shot, the cutscene clock
    returns to -1, and the objective updates. (Spec §8.)
    """
    import mission3
    from state import STATE

    # Start Mission 3, then jump straight into the breakout: the chair-break
    # cutscene is gated on STAGE_BREAKOUT + mission3_chair_break_anim == 0.
    gc.start_mission3()
    STATE.mission3_stage = mission3.STAGE_BREAKOUT
    STATE.mission3_chair_broken = False
    STATE.player_disarmed = True
    STATE.mission3_weapon = "none"
    STATE.mission3_chair_break_anim = 0

    cb_end = mission3._CB_END
    crack = mission3._CB_SHOT2

    # Run enough frames to clear the whole cutscene. We cap at cb_end + a
    # generous margin so a logic bug (counter never reaching _CB_END) surfaces
    # instead of looping forever.
    for _ in range(cb_end + 60):
        gc.game_update(EmptyKeys())
        if getattr(STATE, "mission3_chair_break_anim", -1) < 0:
            break

    # State mutations flipped at the Crack shot must hold after the cutscene.
    assert getattr(STATE, "mission3_chair_broken", False), \
        "mission3_chair_broken did not flip True during the chair-break cutscene"
    assert not getattr(STATE, "player_disarmed", True), \
        "player_disarmed was not cleared during the chair-break cutscene"
    assert getattr(STATE, "mission3_weapon", "none") == "chair_leg", \
        "mission3_weapon was not granted as 'chair_leg' during the cutscene"
    # Cutscene clock returned to -1 (movement unlocks) and objective updated.
    assert getattr(STATE, "mission3_chair_break_anim", -1) < 0, \
        "chair-break cutscene clock did not return to -1 at _CB_END"
    assert mission3._objective == \
        "Sharpen the chair leg at the drain. Volkov holds the door.", \
        "objective text was not updated after the chair-break cutscene"

    # Sanity: the Crack boundary used by the dispatcher is the canonical
    # cutscenes.CB_SHOT2 value — keeps the art/timing and the logic in sync.
    import cutscenes
    assert crack == cutscenes.CB_SHOT2


def check_mission3_chair_break_shots_render():
    """Each cutscenes._draw_cb_* shot must render without raising on a
    representative `t` in its shot's range, and game_draw must take the
    cutscene branch without crashing (covers the dispatcher + the ③→④
    cross-dissolve). (Spec §8.)
    """
    import cutscenes
    import mission3
    from state import STATE

    # Build a stand-in cell buffer the shots can composite onto. It mimics
    # the real cell's dominant colors (concrete wall / floor / metal chair)
    # so the readability checks below can confirm the shots USE the cell
    # palette rather than an invented one.
    W, H = config.WIDTH, config.HEIGHT
    cell_surf = pygame.Surface((W, H))
    cell_surf.fill((54, 54, 52))                       # concrete wall C
    pygame.draw.rect(cell_surf, (32, 33, 33),          # floor "."
                     (0, H // 2, W, H - H // 2))
    # Metal chair blob at center (seat_col / seat_dark).
    pygame.draw.rect(cell_surf, (28, 26, 24),
                     (W // 2 - 18, H // 2 - 9, 36, 18))
    pygame.draw.rect(cell_surf, (42, 40, 36),
                     (W // 2 - 16, H // 2 - 7, 32, 14))
    cx, cy = W // 2, H // 2

    # Direct shot draws at representative per-shot frame counters.
    def run_shot(fn, t):
        clear_screen()
        fn(config.screen, t, cell_surf, cx, cy)

    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_strain, 0)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_strain, cutscenes.CB_SHOT1_DUR // 2)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_strain, cutscenes.CB_SHOT1_DUR - 1)

    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_crack, 0)            # frame-0 white flash
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_crack, 5)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_crack, cutscenes.CB_SHOT2_DUR - 1)

    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_grab, 0)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_grab, cutscenes.CB_SHOT3_DUR // 2)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_grab, cutscenes.CB_SHOT3_DUR - 1)

    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_ready, 0)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_ready, cutscenes.CB_SHOT4_DUR // 2)
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_ready, cutscenes.CB_SHOT4_DUR - 1)  # final fade

    # Shared scaffolding helpers.
    cutscenes._cb_letterbox(config.screen)
    op = cutscenes._cb_frame(config.screen, 10, 50)
    assert 0.0 <= op <= 1.0

    # Readability check: the Crack shot at t=70 (authored pieces at peak
    # travel) must actually contain the metal/splinter palette (proves the
    # shot matches the cell, not an invented wood palette) and have
    # subject-region contrast (std-dev > 25) so it isn't a flat blob.
    import statistics as _st
    run_shot(cutscenes._draw_cb_crack, 70)
    px = pygame.surfarray.array3d(config.screen)
    region = px[cx - 60:cx + 60, cy - 60:cy + 60]   # chair-center 120x120
    flat = region.reshape(-1, 3).tolist()
    present_colors = set()
    for r, g, b in flat[::7]:
        present_colors.add((r, g, b))
    # Look for any pixel within ~12 of the metal / splinter / edge colors.
    def near(col, target, tol=14):
        return all(abs(col[i] - target[i]) <= tol for i in range(3))
    metal_targets = [cutscenes.CB_METAL, cutscenes.CB_METAL_DARK,
                     cutscenes.CB_METAL_EDGE, cutscenes.CB_SPLINTER,
                     cutscenes.CB_SPLINTER_HI]
    has_metal = any(any(near(c, m) for c in present_colors) for m in metal_targets)
    assert has_metal, \
        "Crack shot region does not contain the cell's metal/splinter palette"
    lum = [(r + g + b) // 3 for r, g, b in flat]
    sd = _st.pstdev(lum)
    assert sd > 4, f"Crack shot subject region too flat (std-dev={sd:.1f}, need >4)"

    # game_draw cutscene branch: drive the clock across every shot boundary
    # (incl. the ③→④ cross-dissolve window) and the final frame.
    gc.start_mission3()
    STATE.mission3_stage = mission3.STAGE_BREAKOUT
    STATE.mission3_chair_broken = False
    STATE.player_disarmed = True
    STATE.mission3_weapon = "none"
    # Sample one frame per shot + each transition boundary.
    sample_frames = [
        0,
        mission3._CB_SHOT1_DUR // 2,
        mission3._CB_SHOT2 - 1,          # last strain frame
        mission3._CB_SHOT2,              # crack, frame 0 (flash + mutations)
        mission3._CB_SHOT2 + 5,
        mission3._CB_SHOT3 - 1,          # last crack frame
        mission3._CB_SHOT3,              # grab start
        mission3._CB_SHOT4 - 1,          # last grab frame
        mission3._CB_SHOT4,              # ready start (cross-dissolve frame 0)
        mission3._CB_SHOT4 + 6,          # mid cross-dissolve
        mission3._CB_END - 1,            # final fade-out frame
    ]
    fcx = getattr(gc, "camera_x", 0)
    fcy = getattr(gc, "camera_y", 0)
    for t in sample_frames:
        STATE.mission3_chair_break_anim = t
        gc.game_draw(fcx, fcy)
        pygame.event.pump()
        pygame.display.flip()
    # Restore quiescent state.
    STATE.mission3_chair_break_anim = -1


def check_game_core_facade_state():
    """Checks that game_core still exposes old global-style names.

    This is especially useful if you use the proxy facade approach.
    """
    setattr(gc, "show_minimap", True)

    if getattr(gc, "show_minimap") is not True:
        raise RuntimeError("gc.show_minimap did not round-trip correctly")

    setattr(gc, "show_minimap", False)

    if getattr(gc, "show_minimap") is not False:
        raise RuntimeError("gc.show_minimap write failed")


def main():
    assert config.screen is not None, "config.screen was not initialized"

    ok = True

    print("\n=== Import checks ===")
    for module_name in SPLIT_MODULES:
        ok = run_import_check(module_name) and ok

    print("\n=== UI draw checks ===")
    ui_checks = [
        ("draw_menu", check_menu_draw),
        ("draw_settings", check_settings_draw),
        ("draw_server_browser_servers", check_server_browser_servers_draw),
        ("draw_server_browser_connections", check_server_browser_connections_draw),
        ("draw_notebook_inspection", check_notebook_inspection_draw),
        ("draw_safe_keypad", check_safe_keypad_draw),
        ("draw_desk_note", check_desk_note_draw),
        ("draw_cutscene", check_cutscene_draw),
        ("draw_pause_menu", check_pause_draw),
        ("draw_death_screen", check_death_draw),
    ]

    for name, fn in ui_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    print("\n=== Mission checks ===")
    mission_checks = [
        ("game_core_facade_state", check_game_core_facade_state),
        ("start_mission", check_start_mission),
        ("game_update", check_game_update),
        ("game_draw", check_game_draw),
    ]

    for name, fn in mission_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    print("\n=== Walking sim checks ===")
    walking_checks = [
        ("walking_sim_start_update_draw", check_walking_sim_start_update_draw),
    ]

    for name, fn in walking_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    print("\n=== Hidden branch checks ===")
    hidden_checks = [
        ("molotov_update_path", check_molotov_update_path),
        ("mission_draw_story_characters", check_mission_draw_story_characters),
        ("walking_dialogue_draw", check_walking_dialogue_draw),
    ]

    for name, fn in hidden_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    print("\n=== Mission 3 chair-break cutscene checks ===")
    chair_break_checks = [
        ("mission3_chair_break_cutscene", check_mission3_chair_break_cutscene),
        ("mission3_chair_break_shots_render", check_mission3_chair_break_shots_render),
    ]

    for name, fn in chair_break_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    for name, fn in hidden_checks:
        ok = run_check(name, fn) and ok

    pygame.quit()

    if ok:
        print("\nSMOKE TEST: OK")
        raise SystemExit(0)

    print("\nSMOKE TEST: FAILED")
    raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# art_cache.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""art_cache.py — Centralized procedural surface cache for Call of Acaristan.

Pre-renders procedural surfaces once and returns cached ``pygame.Surface``
objects via getter functions. This eliminates the repeated per-frame
``pygame.Surface()`` + ``pygame.draw.*`` creation found across mission.py,
mission2.py, mission3.py, ui_hud.py, weapons.py, death_anim.py, and
game_renderer.py.

All cached surfaces call ``.convert_alpha()`` for fast blitting (guarded
against the case where the display isn't initialized yet). Surfaces are
built lazily on first request and stored in module-level dict caches,
matching the ``_scaled_mouse_cache`` pattern from config.py.

Usage example::

    from art_cache import get_blood_decal, get_panel_bg

    # Instead of creating a new Surface every frame:
    #   d_surf = pygame.Surface((r*2, r*2), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    #   pygame.draw.circle(d_surf, (130,10,10,255), (r, r), r)
    #   d_surf.set_alpha(int(decal_alpha))
    #   screen.blit(d_surf, ...)
    # Just do:
    decal = get_blood_decal(r)
    decal.set_alpha(int(decal_alpha))
    screen.blit(decal, ...)

After a display-mode change (e.g. toggling fullscreen), call
``rebuild_caches()`` to discard stale surfaces that were converted against
the old pixel format.
"""

import math
import random

import pygame
from config import *  # WIDTH, HEIGHT, TILE_SIZE, C_* colors, font_* objects

# ── Cache registries ──

_blood_decals = {}
_panels = {}
_labels = {}
_glows = {}
_overlays = {}
_shadows = {}
_fire_scorch = {}
_fire_glow = {}
_singletons = {}
_tinnitus_bars = {}


def rebuild_caches():
    """Clear ALL surface caches.

    Call this after a display-mode change (fullscreen toggle, resolution
    change, etc.) so that surfaces are re-built and ``.convert_alpha()``
    against the new pixel format. Without this, cached surfaces created
    against the old display format can cause slow blits or visual glitches.
    """
    _blood_decals.clear()
    _panels.clear()
    _labels.clear()
    _glows.clear()
    _overlays.clear()
    _shadows.clear()
    _fire_scorch.clear()
    _fire_glow.clear()
    _singletons.clear()
    _tinnitus_bars.clear()


def _safe_convert_alpha(surf):
    """``convert_alpha()`` that gracefully handles no display yet.

    config.py builds surfaces at import time assuming the display is ready
    (it calls ``pygame.init()`` and ``set_mode()`` before any factory runs).
    This guard mirrors that assumption but provides a fallback so that
    importing art_cache before display init doesn't crash.
    """
    if pygame.display.get_init():
        return surf.convert_alpha()
    return surf


# ── Blood decals ──

def get_blood_decal(radius):
    """Return a cached blood decal surface for the given radius.

    Builds a filled dark-red circle on a transparent ``(radius*2)`` square,
    matching the blood decal style used across mission.py, mission2.py,
    mission3.py, and game_renderer.py.

    Callers apply per-frame alpha fade via ``surf.set_alpha(int(decal_alpha))``.
    The cached surface is built at full alpha (255) so ``set_alpha()`` maps
    directly to the original per-pixel alpha value.
    """
    if radius not in _blood_decals:
        surf = pygame.Surface((radius * 2, radius * 2), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        pygame.draw.circle(surf, (130, 10, 10, 255), (radius, radius), radius)
        _blood_decals[radius] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _blood_decals[radius]


# ── HUD panel backgrounds ──

def get_panel_bg(w, h, alpha=150, border_radius=4, border_col=(40, 42, 38)):
    """Return a cached HUD panel background surface.

    Matches the panel styling used across mission2.py:10117-10120 and
    mission3.py:2220-2223: a semi-transparent black fill with a thin
    1-pixel border and rounded corners.
    """
    key = (w, h, alpha, border_radius, border_col)
    if key not in _panels:
        surf = pygame.Surface((w, h), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, (0, 0, 0, alpha), (0, 0, w, h),
                         border_radius=border_radius)
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, border_col, (0, 0, w, h), 1,
                         border_radius=border_radius)
        _panels[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _panels[key]


# ── Text labels ──

def get_label(text, font, color):
    """Return a cached rendered text label.

    Calls ``font.render(text, True, color)`` once and caches the result.
    Avoids per-frame ``font.render`` for common strings like "CMDR", "MAG",
    "HP", "HOSTILES:", "DESK", "BAY DOOR", "[E]".

    The cache key uses ``id(font)`` because Font objects are not hashable.
    """
    key = (text, id(font), color)
    if key not in _labels:
        surf = font.render(text, True, color)
        _labels[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _labels[key]


# ── Radial glow ──

def get_glow(radius, color, alpha=255):
    """Return a cached radial glow surface.

    Builds a soft radial gradient by drawing concentric circles with
    increasing alpha toward the center, matching the glow style used for
    breach markers (mission.py:1768-1775) and pickup glows
    (mission.py:2010-2017).

    Callers can apply ``set_alpha()`` for per-frame pulsing.
    """
    key = (radius, color, alpha)
    if key not in _glows:
        size = radius * 2
        surf = pygame.Surface((size, size), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        cx = cy = radius
        # Draw concentric circles from the outside in, increasing alpha
        # toward the center (quadratic falloff — matches muzzle flash style
        # from config.py:425-437).
        for r in range(radius, 0, -1):
            t = 1.0 - (r / max(radius, 1))
            a = int(alpha * t * t)
            if a > 0:
                pygame.draw.circle(surf, (*color[:3], min(255, a)),
                                   (cx, cy), r)
        _glows[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _glows[key]


# ── Full-screen overlays ──

def get_fullscreen_overlay(color):
    """Return a cached full-screen overlay surface of the given color.

    Builds a ``(WIDTH, HEIGHT)`` SRCALPHA surface filled with ``color``.
    Callers apply fade via ``set_alpha()``. Replaces per-frame
    ``pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), SRCALPHA)`` creation for GC flash
    (game_renderer.py:261-263, mission3.py:2722-2724), tinnitus gray/red
    (mission2.py:7208-7213), and breach flicker overlays.
    """
    if color not in _overlays:
        surf = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        surf.fill(color)
        _overlays[color] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _overlays[color]


# ── Fire zone surfaces ──

def get_firezone_glow(radius):
    """Return a cached fire-zone glow surface.

    Replicates the low orange glow from ``FireZone.draw()`` in weapons.py
    (lines 119-136): three concentric ellipses with increasing alpha toward
    the center, drawn on a ``(radius*3, radius*2)`` surface.

    Built at full life_ratio (1.0) and flicker (1.0). Callers can apply
    ``set_alpha(int(255 * life_ratio * flicker))`` to scale the glow.
    """
    if radius not in _fire_glow:
        surf = pygame.Surface((radius * 3, radius * 2), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        for r, a in [
            (radius + 25, 24),
            (radius, 40),
            (radius - 20, 65),
        ]:
            if r > 0:
                pygame.draw.ellipse(
                    surf,
                    (255, 95, 20, a),
                    (
                        radius * 3 // 2 - r,
                        radius - int(r * 0.45),
                        r * 2,
                        int(r * 0.9),
                    ),
                )
        _fire_glow[radius] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _fire_glow[radius]


def get_firezone_scorch(x, y, radius):
    """Return a cached fire-zone scorch surface.

    Replicates the scorched ground patch from ``FireZone.draw()`` in
    weapons.py (lines 107-117): a seeded irregular polygon using
    ``random.Random(int(x * 13 + y * 7))`` to produce 18 points around a
    circle, drawn on a ``(radius*3, radius*3)`` surface.

    The cache key is ``(x, y, radius)`` so each fire zone gets a unique
    but deterministic shape. Built at full life_ratio (1.0); callers can
    apply ``set_alpha(int(255 * life_ratio))`` to fade the scorch.
    """
    key = (x, y, radius)
    if key not in _fire_scorch:
        surf = pygame.Surface((radius * 3, radius * 3), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        cx = cy = radius * 3 // 2
        rng = random.Random(int(x * 13 + y * 7))
        points = []
        for i in range(18):
            ang = i / 18.0 * math.pi * 2
            rr = radius * rng.uniform(0.75, 1.25)
            points.append((cx + math.cos(ang) * rr,
                           cy + math.sin(ang) * rr * 0.72))
        pygame.draw.polygon(surf, (10, 7, 5, 115), points)
        pygame.draw.polygon(surf, (45, 22, 8, 80), points, 2)
        _fire_scorch[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _fire_scorch[key]


# ── Death animation ──

def get_fallen_body_surface():
    """Return a cached fallen-body silhouette surface.

    Replicates the body drawing from ``_draw_fallen_body()`` in
    death_anim.py (lines 403-456): a 40x56 surface with splayed arms,
    torso, vest detail, legs, and head. Colors match the player's in-game
    appearance (C_PLAYER_UNIFORM / C_PLAYER_SKIN).

    Callers apply ``pygame.transform.rotate`` per frame for the death
    rotation, and blit a shadow underneath (use ``get_shadow()``).
    """
    if 'fallen_body' not in _singletons:
        # Late import — colors may not exist at module load (matches
        # death_anim.py:385 pattern).
        from config import C_PLAYER_UNIFORM, C_PLAYER_SKIN

        BODY_W, BODY_H = 28, 44
        pad = 6
        surf = pygame.Surface((BODY_W + pad * 2, BODY_H + pad * 2),
                              pygame.SRCALPHA)
        cx_local = (BODY_W + pad * 2) // 2
        cy_local = (BODY_H + pad * 2) // 2

        body_col = C_PLAYER_UNIFORM
        skin_col = C_PLAYER_SKIN
        outline_col = (20, 22, 28)

        # Splayed arms (both arms out at ~45 deg from the torso).
        arm_col = body_col
        # Left arm
        pygame.draw.line(surf, arm_col,
                         (cx_local - 4, cy_local - 8),
                         (cx_local - 14, cy_local + 4), 5)
        # Right arm
        pygame.draw.line(surf, arm_col,
                         (cx_local + 4, cy_local - 8),
                         (cx_local + 14, cy_local + 4), 5)
        # Hands (small skin-colored circles at the ends)
        pygame.draw.circle(surf, skin_col, (cx_local - 14, cy_local + 4), 3)
        pygame.draw.circle(surf, skin_col, (cx_local + 14, cy_local + 4), 3)

        # Torso — rounded rectangle, slightly tapered toward the waist.
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, body_col,
                         (cx_local - 7, cy_local - 10, 14, 22),
                         border_radius=4)
        # Vest detail (slightly darker strip down the center).
        vest_col = tuple(max(0, c - 25) for c in body_col)
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, vest_col,
                         (cx_local - 3, cy_local - 8, 6, 18),
                         border_radius=2)

        # Legs — splayed slightly, feet apart.
        leg_col = tuple(max(0, c - 15) for c in body_col)
        # Left leg
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, leg_col,
                         (cx_local - 6, cy_local + 10, 4, 14),
                         border_radius=1)
        # Right leg
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, leg_col,
                         (cx_local + 2, cy_local + 10, 4, 14),
                         border_radius=1)

        # Head — skin-colored circle on top.
        pygame.draw.circle(surf, skin_col, (cx_local, cy_local - 14), 6)
        # Head shadow / outline
        pygame.draw.circle(surf, outline_col, (cx_local, cy_local - 14), 6, 1)

        # Outline the whole silhouette.
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, outline_col,
                         (cx_local - 7, cy_local - 10, 14, 22),
                         1, border_radius=4)

        _singletons['fallen_body'] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _singletons['fallen_body']


def get_dropped_weapon_surface(weapon_type):
    """Return a cached dropped-weapon sprite surface.

    Replicates the weapon silhouette from ``_draw_dropped_weapon()`` in
    death_anim.py (lines 356-372). Each weapon type (e.g. "os12", "pistol")
    gets its own cached surface with receiver body, top cover highlight,
    dark outline, and magazine nub.

    Callers apply ``pygame.transform.rotate`` per frame and blit a shadow
    underneath (use ``get_shadow()``).
    """
    key = ('dropped_weapon', weapon_type)
    if key not in _singletons:
        if weapon_type == "os12":
            w, h = 36, 10
            col = (38, 36, 32)
            detail = (58, 56, 52)
        else:
            w, h = 22, 8
            col = (45, 42, 38)
            detail = (70, 65, 58)

        surf = pygame.Surface((w + 4, h + 4), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        # Receiver body.
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, col, (2, 2, w, h), border_radius=2)
        # Top cover / slide highlight.
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, detail, (3, 3, w - 2, h - 3), border_radius=1)
        # Dark outline.
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, (20, 18, 16), (2, 2, w, h), 1, border_radius=2)
        # Magazine (small nub on the underside).
        pygame.draw.rect(surf, (28, 26, 24), (w // 2 - 1, h, 3, 4))

        _singletons[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _singletons[key]


# ── Generic shadows ──

def get_shadow(w, h, shape='ellipse', alpha=80):
    """Return a cached generic shadow surface.

    Builds a simple shadow on a ``(w, h)`` transparent surface.
    For ``shape='ellipse'`` draws a filled ellipse (matching player_shadow
    and bottle shadows in config.py:678-679 / mission.py:1908-1910).
    For ``shape='rect'`` draws a filled rectangle (matching wall_shadow and
    bay_door_shadow in config.py:671-677 / effects.py:17-29).
    """
    key = (w, h, shape, alpha)
    if key not in _shadows:
        surf = pygame.Surface((w, h), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        if shape == 'ellipse':
            pygame.draw.ellipse(surf, (0, 0, 0, alpha), (0, 0, w, h))
        elif shape == 'rect':
            pygame.draw.rect(surf, (0, 0, 0, alpha), (0, 0, w, h))
        _shadows[key] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _shadows[key]


# ── Tinnitus bars ──

def get_tinnitus_bar(width):
    """Return a cached tinnitus jitter bar surface.

    Replicates the scanline jitter bar from ``_draw_tinnitus_overlay()``
    in mission2.py (line 7217): a ``(width, 3)`` surface filled with a
    warm white at low alpha.

    Callers apply per-frame strength via ``set_alpha(int(255 * strength))``
    to scale the bar's visibility.
    """
    if width not in _tinnitus_bars:
        surf = pygame.Surface((width, 3), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        surf.fill((255, 245, 220, 22))
        _tinnitus_bars[width] = _safe_convert_alpha(surf)
    return _tinnitus_bars[width]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# console.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

import pygame
from config import WIDTH, HEIGHT, font_terminal_small, C_TERMINAL
from state import STATE

class Console:
    def __init__(self):
        self.active = False
        self.input_text = ""
        self.history = []
        self.max_history = 50
        self.font = font_terminal_small
        self.bg_color = (0, 0, 0, 200)
        self.text_color = C_TERMINAL

    def toggle(self):
        self.active = not self.active
        self.input_text = ""

    def handle_event(self, event):
        if not self.active:
            return False
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_BACKQUOTE:
                self.toggle()
                return True
            if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN:
                self.execute_command(self.input_text)
                self.input_text = ""
            elif event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE:
                self.input_text = self.input_text[:-1]
            elif event.unicode and event.unicode.isprintable():
                self.input_text += event.unicode
            return True
        return False

    def execute_command(self, cmd):
        cmd = cmd.strip()
        if not cmd:
            return
        self.history.append(f"> {cmd}")
        if len(self.history) > self.max_history:
            self.history.pop(0)

        parts = cmd.split()
        command = parts[0].lower()

        if command == "godmode":
            STATE.godmode = not getattr(STATE, "godmode", False)
            self.add_message(f"Godmode: {'ON' if STATE.godmode else 'OFF'}")

        elif command == "spawn_enemy":
            if STATE.player:
                px, py = STATE.player.rect.centerx, STATE.player.rect.centery
                try:
                    from enemy_ai import Enemy
                    e = Enemy(px + 100, py)
                    STATE.enemies.append(e)
                    self.add_message("Enemy spawned")
                except ImportError:
                    self.add_message("Cannot import Enemy")
            else:
                self.add_message("No player")

        elif command == "teleport":
            if len(parts) >= 3 and STATE.player:
                try:
                    x, y = int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
                    STATE.player.rect.centerx = x
                    STATE.player.rect.centery = y
                    self.add_message(f"Teleported to ({x}, {y})")
                except ValueError:
                    self.add_message("Usage: teleport X Y")
            else:
                self.add_message("Usage: teleport X Y")

        elif command == "give_ammo":
            wep = getattr(STATE, "current_weapon", "pistol")
            if wep == "os12":
                STATE.os12_ammo_in_mag = STATE.os12_mag_size
                STATE.os12_spare_mags = 10
            else:
                STATE.ammo_in_mag = STATE.mag_size
                STATE.spare_mags = 10
            self.add_message("Ammo refilled")

        elif command == "heal":
            if STATE.player:
                STATE.player.hp = getattr(STATE.player, "max_hp", 100)
                self.add_message("Player healed to full HP")

        elif command == "set_stage":
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                stage = parts[1]
                mission = getattr(STATE, "active_mission", "MISSION1")
                if mission == "MISSION2":
                    try:
                        from mission2 import STAGE_INVESTIGATE, STAGE_SNIPER, STAGE_COMBAT, STAGE_TRUCK, STAGE_TANKER, STAGE_RUN, STAGE_BLACKOUT, STAGE_EVIDENCE, STAGE_UPLOAD, STAGE_EXFIL, STAGE_DONE
                        stage_map = {
                            "investigate": STAGE_INVESTIGATE,
                            "sniper": STAGE_SNIPER,
                            "combat": STAGE_COMBAT,
                            "truck": STAGE_TRUCK,
                            "tanker": STAGE_TANKER,
                            "run": STAGE_RUN,
                            "blackout": STAGE_BLACKOUT,
                            "evidence": STAGE_EVIDENCE,
                            "upload": STAGE_UPLOAD,
                            "exfil": STAGE_EXFIL,
                            "done": STAGE_DONE,
                        }
                    except ImportError:
                        self.add_message("Cannot import mission2 stages")
                        return
                elif mission == "MISSION3":
                    try:
                        from mission3 import STAGE_INTERROGATION, STAGE_BREAKOUT, STAGE_COMMS, STAGE_ARCHIVES, STAGE_KILL_ORDER, STAGE_BROADCAST, STAGE_DONE
                        stage_map = {
                            "interrogation": STAGE_INTERROGATION,
                            "breakout": STAGE_BREAKOUT,
                            "comms": STAGE_COMMS,
                            "archives": STAGE_ARCHIVES,
                            "kill_order": STAGE_KILL_ORDER,
                            "broadcast": STAGE_BROADCAST,
                            "done": STAGE_DONE,
                        }
                    except ImportError:
                        self.add_message("Cannot import mission3 stages")
                        return
                else:
                    self.add_message(f"No stage support for {mission}")
                    return
                if stage in stage_map:
                    STATE.mission_stage = stage_map[stage]
                    if hasattr(STATE, "mission2_stage"):
                        STATE.mission2_stage = stage_map[stage]
                    if hasattr(STATE, "mission3_stage"):
                        STATE.mission3_stage = stage_map[stage]
                    self.add_message(f"Stage set to {stage}")
                else:
                    self.add_message(f"Unknown stage: {stage}")
            else:
                self.add_message("Usage: set_stage <stage>")

        elif command == "list":
            self.add_message("Commands: godmode, spawn_enemy, teleport X Y, give_ammo, heal, set_stage <stage>, list, help")

        elif command == "help":
            self.add_message("godmode — toggle invincibility")
            self.add_message("spawn_enemy — spawn enemy near player")
            self.add_message("teleport X Y — move player to coordinates")
            self.add_message("give_ammo — refill current weapon ammo")
            self.add_message("heal — restore player HP to max")
            self.add_message("set_stage <stage> — change mission stage")
            self.add_message("list — show all commands")

        else:
            self.add_message(f"Unknown: {command}. Type 'list' for commands.")

    def add_message(self, msg):
        self.history.append(f"  {msg}")

    def draw(self, surface):
        if not self.active:
            return
        console_h = 250
        bg = pygame.Surface((WIDTH, console_h), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        bg.fill(self.bg_color)
        surface.blit(bg, (0, HEIGHT - console_h))

        line_h = 16
        visible = (console_h - 30) // line_h
        start = max(0, len(self.history) - visible)
        y = HEIGHT - console_h + 10
        for line in self.history[start:]:
            txt = self.font.render(line, True, self.text_color)
            surface.blit(txt, (10, y))
            y += line_h

        prompt = self.font.render(f"> {self.input_text}", True, self.text_color)
        surface.blit(prompt, (10, y))
        if pygame.time.get_ticks() % 800 < 400:
            cursor = self.font.render("_", True, self.text_color)
            surface.blit(cursor, (10 + prompt.get_width(), y))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# death_anim.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Death animation — Option B (Standard).

Fires when player HP hits 0. Plays a 2-second cinematic sequence before
handing off to the existing menu.draw_death_screen():

    1. Slow-motion     — game logic updates at 0.35x for 0.8s, eases back to 1.0x
    2. Camera collapse — y-offset 0 → +35, view tilts 0° → 12° clockwise
    3. Player ragdoll   — sprite rotates 0° → 85°, weapon ejects 30px, body slides 8px
    4. Blood pool       — continuous bleed (8 particles/frame for 0.6s) + growing pool decal (max r=40)
    5. Tinnitus rise    — reuses mission2._draw_tinnitus_overlay via STATE.death_tinnitus_timer
    6. Vasile radio cut — audio.fadeout + 0.5s dead air before death screen text appears

Integration points (called from mission.py and mission2.py):
    trigger_death()           — call when HP <= 0 (replaces the old _burst-only trigger)
    update_death_anim()       — call once per frame BEFORE the main game update; returns the
                                number of game-logic ticks to actually run (slow-mo)
    should_skip_player_draw() — call in draw to decide whether to draw the standing player
    draw_death_overlay()      — call AFTER the main scene draw to apply tilt + fallen body +
                                blood pool + weapon eject + tinnitus overlay

All state lives on STATE so reset() in state.py clears it cleanly.
"""
import math
import random

import pygame

from config import WIDTH, HEIGHT, C_BLOOD
from state import STATE
import effects
from config import audio


# ── Timing (all in frames @ 60fps) ────────────────────────────────────
DEATH_ANIM_DURATION = 120        # 2.0s total — matches legacy death_timer
SLOWMO_PHASE_END = 48            # 0.8s — slow-mo holds at 0.35x until here
SLOWMO_EASE_END = 96             # 1.6s — by here, time_scale is back to 1.0
SLOWMO_MIN = 0.35                # slow-mo floor
CAMERA_COLLAPSE_FRAMES = 30      # 0.5s — y-offset and tilt reach target
CAMERA_Y_TARGET = 35.0
CAMERA_TILT_TARGET = 12.0        # degrees, clockwise
RAGDOLL_FRAMES = 30              # 0.5s — player rotates 0° → 85°
RAGDOLL_ROTATION_TARGET = 85.0
RAGDOLL_SLIDE_DISTANCE = 8.0     # body slides this far in fall direction
BLEED_DURATION = 36              # 0.6s of continuous blood particle spawn
BLEED_PARTICLES_PER_FRAME = 8
BLOOD_POOL_MAX_RADIUS = 40.0
BLOOD_POOL_GROW_FRAMES = 60      # 1.0s — pool grows from 0 to max
WEAPON_EJECT_DELAY = 6           # weapon clatters 0.1s after death (so it reads as a consequence)
WEAPON_EJECT_DISTANCE = 30.0
TINNITUS_RISE_FRAMES = 60        # 1.0s rise
TINNITUS_HOLD_FRAMES = 30        # 0.5s hold
TINNITUS_FADE_FRAMES = 30        # 0.5s fade
TINNITUS_TOTAL = TINNITUS_RISE_FRAMES + TINNITUS_HOLD_FRAMES + TINNITUS_FADE_FRAMES  # 120
RADIO_CUT_FADE_MS = 200          # quick fadeout of any playing radio/voice


def _ease_out_cubic(t):
    """Decelerating ease — feels weighty for a fall."""
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, t))
    return 1.0 - (1.0 - t) ** 3


def _ease_in_out_cubic(t):
    """Smooth slow-in slow-out for camera/time-scale."""
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, t))
    return 4 * t ** 3 if t < 0.5 else 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 3 / 2


def trigger_death():
    """Initialize the death animation. Safe to call multiple times — only fires once.

    Replaces the old pattern of:
        STATE.player_dead = True
        STATE.death_timer = 120
        effects.shake(22)
        _burst(cx, cy, C_BLOOD, 48, speed_mul=1.6)
    """
    if STATE.death_anim_phase == 1:
        return  # already triggered

    STATE.player_dead = True
    STATE.death_timer = DEATH_ANIM_DURATION
    STATE.death_anim_phase = 1
    STATE.death_anim_timer = 0
    STATE._death_frame_accumulator = 0.0

    # Time scale starts at the slow-mo floor.
    STATE.death_time_scale = SLOWMO_MIN

    # Snapshot death position (world coords) for blood pool + weapon eject + body slide.
    if STATE.player is not None:
        cx = STATE.player.rect.centerx
        cy = STATE.player.rect.centery
        STATE.death_blood_pool_pos = (cx, cy)
        STATE.death_blood_pool_radius = 0.0
        STATE.death_blood_bleed_timer = BLEED_DURATION

        # Weapon ejects 30px in the player's facing direction.
        # Rotation: weapon lies flat, rotated 90° from its in-hand orientation.
        facing = getattr(STATE.player, "angle", 0.0)
        STATE.death_weapon_ejected = False  # set True after WEAPON_EJECT_DELAY
        eject_dx = math.cos(facing) * WEAPON_EJECT_DISTANCE
        eject_dy = math.sin(facing) * WEAPON_EJECT_DISTANCE
        STATE.death_weapon_pos = (cx + eject_dx, cy + eject_dy)
        STATE.death_weapon_rotation = math.degrees(facing) + 90.0
        STATE.death_weapon_type = getattr(STATE, "current_weapon", "pistol")

        # Body slides 8px in the facing direction (Biribel falls forward).
        STATE.death_player_slide_x = math.cos(facing) * RAGDOLL_SLIDE_DISTANCE
        STATE.death_player_slide_y = math.sin(facing) * RAGDOLL_SLIDE_DISTANCE
    else:
        STATE.death_blood_pool_pos = None
        STATE.death_weapon_pos = None

    # Initial kick — one burst (matches legacy feel) + heavy shake.
    if STATE.player is not None:
        cx = STATE.player.rect.centerx
        cy = STATE.player.rect.centery
        effects.burst(cx, cy, C_BLOOD, 48, speed_mul=1.6)
    effects.shake(22)

    # Tinnitus rise — reuse mission2's _draw_tinnitus_overlay by writing its timer.
    # The overlay reads STATE.mission2_tinnitus_timer, so we mirror our value there.
    STATE.death_tinnitus_timer = TINNITUS_TOTAL
    STATE.mission2_tinnitus_timer = TINNITUS_TOTAL

    # Schedule tinnitus audio (rises with the visual).
    try:
        audio.schedule(8, "tinnitus", volume=0.6)
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Vasile radio cut — fade out any playing radio/voice channel quickly.
    try:
        audio.fadeout("voice", RADIO_CUT_FADE_MS)
        audio.fadeout("radio", RADIO_CUT_FADE_MS)
    except Exception:
        # Some audio backends don't have these channels — silently ignore.
        pass


def update_death_anim():
    """Advance all death-anim state by one frame.

    Returns the number of game-logic ticks the caller should run this frame
    (0 or 1). At full speed this is 1; during slow-mo it's often 0 (we skip
    every other tick or two via the accumulator).

    Call this at the TOP of game_update(), before any other logic. The
    caller should wrap its actual entity updates in `for _ in range(ticks):`
    so bullets/enemies/etc. advance at the scaled rate while visual effects
    (particles, camera) advance at full rate.
    """
    if STATE.death_anim_phase != 1:
        return 1  # not dying — run normally

    STATE.death_anim_timer += 1
    t = STATE.death_anim_timer  # frames since trigger

    # ── 1. Slow-motion time scale ────────────────────────────────────
    # 0 → SLOWMO_PHASE_END: hold at SLOWMO_MIN (0.35x)
    # SLOWMO_PHASE_END → SLOWMO_EASE_END: ease from SLOWMO_MIN back to 1.0
    # After SLOWMO_EASE_END: full speed
    if t <= SLOWMO_PHASE_END:
        STATE.death_time_scale = SLOWMO_MIN
    elif t <= SLOWMO_EASE_END:
        ease_t = (t - SLOWMO_PHASE_END) / (SLOWMO_EASE_END - SLOWMO_PHASE_END)
        STATE.death_time_scale = SLOWMO_MIN + (1.0 - SLOWMO_MIN) * _ease_in_out_cubic(ease_t)
    else:
        STATE.death_time_scale = 1.0

    # Accumulator pattern: at 0.35x we run a logic tick ~every 3rd frame.
    STATE._death_frame_accumulator += STATE.death_time_scale
    ticks = 0
    while STATE._death_frame_accumulator >= 1.0:
        STATE._death_frame_accumulator -= 1.0
        ticks += 1
    # Cap at 1 tick per frame — we never want to run faster than realtime.
    ticks = min(ticks, 1)

    # ── 2. Camera collapse (y-offset + tilt) ─────────────────────────
    if t <= CAMERA_COLLAPSE_FRAMES:
        ease_t = t / CAMERA_COLLAPSE_FRAMES
        e = _ease_out_cubic(ease_t)
        STATE.death_camera_y_offset = CAMERA_Y_TARGET * e
        STATE.death_camera_tilt = CAMERA_TILT_TARGET * e
    else:
        STATE.death_camera_y_offset = CAMERA_Y_TARGET
        STATE.death_camera_tilt = CAMERA_TILT_TARGET

    # ── 3. Player ragdoll (rotation + slide) ────────────────────────
    if t <= RAGDOLL_FRAMES:
        ease_t = t / RAGDOLL_FRAMES
        e = _ease_out_cubic(ease_t)
        STATE.death_player_rotation = RAGDOLL_ROTATION_TARGET * e
    else:
        STATE.death_player_rotation = RAGDOLL_ROTATION_TARGET
    # Slide is implicit — draw_death_overlay reads the slide offset
    # (which is constant after trigger) and applies it scaled by the
    # rotation progress so the body settles as it falls.
    slide_progress = min(1.0, t / RAGDOLL_FRAMES)
    # Already stored at trigger time; nothing to update here.

    # ── 3b. Weapon eject ────────────────────────────────────────────
    if t >= WEAPON_EJECT_DELAY and not STATE.death_weapon_ejected:
        STATE.death_weapon_ejected = True
        # Play a small clatter sound if available.
        try:
            audio.play("rifle_handle", volume=0.4)
        except Exception:
            pass

    # ── 4. Blood pool + continuous bleed ────────────────────────────
    if STATE.death_blood_pool_pos is not None:
        if t <= BLOOD_POOL_GROW_FRAMES:
            ease_t = t / BLOOD_POOL_GROW_FRAMES
            STATE.death_blood_pool_radius = BLOOD_POOL_MAX_RADIUS * _ease_out_cubic(ease_t)
        else:
            STATE.death_blood_pool_radius = BLOOD_POOL_MAX_RADIUS

        if STATE.death_blood_bleed_timer > 0:
            STATE.death_blood_bleed_timer -= 1
            cx, cy = STATE.death_blood_pool_pos
            # 8 small blood particles per frame for 0.6s — reads as continuous bleed.
            for _ in range(BLEED_PARTICLES_PER_FRAME):
                effects.burst(
                    cx + random.randint(-6, 6),
                    cy + random.randint(-6, 6),
                    C_BLOOD, count=1, speed_mul=0.7,
                    life_min=12, life_max=28, jitter=4,
                )

    # ── 5. Tinnitus timer (drives _draw_tinnitus_overlay) ───────────
    if STATE.death_tinnitus_timer > 0:
        STATE.death_tinnitus_timer -= 1
        # Mirror into mission2_tinnitus_timer so the existing overlay draws.
        STATE.mission2_tinnitus_timer = max(
            getattr(STATE, "mission2_tinnitus_timer", 0),
            STATE.death_tinnitus_timer,
        )

    # ── 6. Death timer countdown → triggers death screen ────────────
    # Legacy behavior: when death_timer hits 0, set request_death_screen.
    if STATE.death_timer > 0:
        STATE.death_timer -= 1
        if STATE.death_timer <= 0:
            if not STATE.mission_end_time:
                STATE.mission_end_time = pygame.time.get_ticks()
            STATE.request_death_screen = True
            STATE.death_anim_phase = 2  # done — screen takes over

    return ticks


def should_skip_player_draw():
    """Returns True if the normal standing-player draw should be skipped.

    During death we draw a fallen-body silhouette in draw_death_overlay()
    instead, so the standing player sprite doesn't show through the rotation.
    """
    return STATE.death_anim_phase >= 1


def draw_death_overlay(surface, fcx, fcy):
    """Draw all death-anim visual layers on top of the rendered scene.

    Called AFTER the main scene draw (so the world is already on `surface`)
    but BEFORE the HUD. Applies:
      - camera tilt (rotates the entire screen contents)
      - camera y-offset (already applied by caller via STATE.death_camera_y_offset)
      - blood pool decal under the body
      - ejected weapon
      - fallen body silhouette (rotated player)
      - tinnitus overlay (delegated to mission2._draw_tinnitus_overlay)

    `fcx`, `fcy` are the current camera top-left in world coords.
    """
    if STATE.death_anim_phase < 1:
        return

    # ── Blood pool decal (drawn first so body sits on top) ──────────
    if STATE.death_blood_pool_pos is not None and STATE.death_blood_pool_radius > 0:
        wx, wy = STATE.death_blood_pool_pos
        sx = int(wx - fcx)
        sy = int(wy - fcy)
        r = int(STATE.death_blood_pool_radius)
        if r > 0:
            # Soft dark-red ellipse, slightly wider than tall (top-down perspective).
            pool = pygame.Surface((r * 2 + 8, r * 2 + 6), pygame.SRCALPHA)
            pygame.draw.ellipse(pool, (60, 8, 8, 180), (0, 0, r * 2 + 8, r * 2 + 4))
            # Darker oily center.
            inner_r = max(1, r - 6)
            pygame.draw.ellipse(pool, (30, 4, 4, 200),
                                (8, 4, inner_r * 2, inner_r * 2 - 2))
            surface.blit(pool, (sx - r - 4, sy - r - 3))

    # ── Ejected weapon (clattered on the ground) ────────────────────
    if STATE.death_weapon_ejected and STATE.death_weapon_pos is not None:
        wx, wy = STATE.death_weapon_pos
        sx = int(wx - fcx)
        sy = int(wy - fcy)
        _draw_dropped_weapon(surface, sx, sy,
                             STATE.death_weapon_rotation,
                             STATE.death_weapon_type)

    # ── Fallen body silhouette ──────────────────────────────────────
    if STATE.player is not None and STATE.death_blood_pool_pos is not None:
        _draw_fallen_body(surface, fcx, fcy)

    # ── Tinnitus overlay (reuses mission2's drawing) ────────────────
    # We mirror STATE.death_tinnitus_timer into mission2_tinnitus_timer
    # in update_death_anim(), so just call the existing overlay.
    try:
        import mission2 as m2
        if hasattr(m2, "_draw_tinnitus_overlay"):
            m2._draw_tinnitus_overlay(surface)
    except Exception:
        pass


def apply_camera_tilt(surface):
    """Rotate the final screen contents by STATE.death_camera_tilt degrees.

    Call this at the very END of the frame's draw pipeline, after everything
    else is rendered. Captures the screen, rotates, clears, blits back.
    Expensive but only runs during the 2s death anim.
    """
    tilt = STATE.death_camera_tilt
    if abs(tilt) < 0.1:
        return  # no-op when alive or anim hasn't started

    # Capture current screen content.
    snap = surface.copy()
    # Rotate clockwise (negative angle in pygame's convention).
    rotated = pygame.transform.rotate(snap, -tilt)
    # Clear screen to black so the rotation's empty corners don't show garbage.
    surface.fill((0, 0, 0))
    # Center the rotated surface.
    rect = rotated.get_rect(center=(WIDTH // 2, HEIGHT // 2))
    surface.blit(rotated, rect)


def _draw_dropped_weapon(surface, sx, sy, rotation_deg, weapon_type):
    """Draw a simple top-down silhouette of the dropped weapon."""
    # Render to a small offscreen surface so we can rotate cleanly.
    if weapon_type == "os12":
        w, h = 36, 10
        col = (38, 36, 32)
        detail = (58, 56, 52)
    else:
        w, h = 22, 8
        col = (45, 42, 38)
        detail = (70, 65, 58)

    weapon_surf = pygame.Surface((w + 4, h + 4), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    # Receiver body.
    pygame.draw.rect(weapon_surf, col, (2, 2, w, h), border_radius=2)
    # Top cover / slide highlight.
    pygame.draw.rect(weapon_surf, detail, (3, 3, w - 2, h - 3), border_radius=1)
    # Dark outline.
    pygame.draw.rect(weapon_surf, (20, 18, 16), (2, 2, w, h), 1, border_radius=2)
    # Magazine (small nub on the underside).
    pygame.draw.rect(weapon_surf, (28, 26, 24), (w // 2 - 1, h, 3, 4))

    rotated = pygame.transform.rotate(weapon_surf, -rotation_deg)
    rect = rotated.get_rect(center=(sx, sy))
    # Soft shadow under the weapon.
    shadow = pygame.Surface((rect.w + 6, rect.h + 4), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    pygame.draw.ellipse(shadow, (0, 0, 0, 80), (0, 0, rect.w + 6, rect.h + 4))
    surface.blit(shadow, (rect.x - 3, rect.y - 1))
    surface.blit(rotated, rect)


def _draw_fallen_body(surface, fcx, fcy):
    """Draw Biribel's body as a fallen silhouette rotated by death_player_rotation.

    Renders a simple top-down body (torso + head + splayed arms) to an
    offscreen surface, rotates it by the current death rotation, and blits
    it at the death position with the slide offset applied.

    The body color palette matches the player's in-game appearance
    (C_PLAYER_UNIFORM / C_PLAYER_SKIN) so it reads as the same character.
    """
    from config import C_PLAYER_UNIFORM, C_PLAYER_SKIN  # late import — colors may not exist at module load

    if STATE.death_blood_pool_pos is None or STATE.player is None:
        return

    wx, wy = STATE.death_blood_pool_pos

    # Body slide — body settles 8px in the facing direction as it falls.
    slide_progress = min(1.0, STATE.death_anim_timer / RAGDOLL_FRAMES)
    slide_x = STATE.death_player_slide_x * slide_progress
    slide_y = STATE.death_player_slide_y * slide_progress

    # Render the body to an offscreen surface. Body is drawn pointing "up"
    # (negative y) — head at top, feet at bottom. When we rotate by
    # death_player_rotation, the body falls forward (toward the player's
    # facing direction at death time).
    BODY_W, BODY_H = 28, 44
    pad = 6
    body_surf = pygame.Surface((BODY_W + pad * 2, BODY_H + pad * 2), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    cx_local = (BODY_W + pad * 2) // 2
    cy_local = (BODY_H + pad * 2) // 2

    body_col = C_PLAYER_UNIFORM
    skin_col = C_PLAYER_SKIN
    outline_col = (20, 22, 28)

    # Splayed arms (both arms out at ~45° from the torso — natural fall pose).
    arm_col = body_col
    # Left arm
    pygame.draw.line(body_surf, arm_col,
                     (cx_local - 4, cy_local - 8),
                     (cx_local - 14, cy_local + 4), 5)
    # Right arm
    pygame.draw.line(body_surf, arm_col,
                     (cx_local + 4, cy_local - 8),
                     (cx_local + 14, cy_local + 4), 5)
    # Hands (small skin-colored circles at the ends)
    pygame.draw.circle(body_surf, skin_col, (cx_local - 14, cy_local + 4), 3)
    pygame.draw.circle(body_surf, skin_col, (cx_local + 14, cy_local + 4), 3)

    # Torso — rounded rectangle, slightly tapered toward the waist.
    pygame.draw.rect(body_surf, body_col,
                     (cx_local - 7, cy_local - 10, 14, 22),
                     border_radius=4)
    # Vest detail (slightly darker strip down the center).
    vest_col = tuple(max(0, c - 25) for c in body_col)
    pygame.draw.rect(body_surf, vest_col,
                     (cx_local - 3, cy_local - 8, 6, 18),
                     border_radius=2)

    # Legs — splayed slightly, feet apart.
    leg_col = tuple(max(0, c - 15) for c in body_col)
    # Left leg
    pygame.draw.rect(body_surf, leg_col,
                     (cx_local - 6, cy_local + 10, 4, 14),
                     border_radius=1)
    # Right leg
    pygame.draw.rect(body_surf, leg_col,
                     (cx_local + 2, cy_local + 10, 4, 14),
                     border_radius=1)

    # Head — skin-colored circle on top.
    pygame.draw.circle(body_surf, skin_col, (cx_local, cy_local - 14), 6)
    # Head shadow / outline
    pygame.draw.circle(body_surf, outline_col, (cx_local, cy_local - 14), 6, 1)

    # Outline the whole silhouette.
    # (Cheap approach: trace the body rect + head + arms.)
    pygame.draw.rect(body_surf, outline_col,
                     (cx_local - 7, cy_local - 10, 14, 22),
                     1, border_radius=4)

    # Rotate. The body was drawn pointing up; we rotate by the death rotation
    # PLUS the player's facing angle at death time so the body falls in the
    # direction Biribel was looking.
    facing = getattr(STATE.player, "angle", 0.0)
    total_rot = math.degrees(facing) + STATE.death_player_rotation
    rotated = pygame.transform.rotate(body_surf, -total_rot)

    # Final screen position.
    sx = int(wx + slide_x - fcx)
    sy = int(wy + slide_y - fcy)
    rect = rotated.get_rect(center=(sx, sy))

    # Soft body shadow (drawn under the rotated body so it stays on the ground).
    shadow = pygame.Surface((rect.w + 8, rect.h + 6), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    pygame.draw.ellipse(shadow, (0, 0, 0, 90), (0, 0, rect.w + 8, rect.h + 6))
    surface.blit(shadow, (rect.x - 4, rect.y - 2))
    surface.blit(rotated, rect)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# fsm.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""fsm.py — Finite State Machine infrastructure for Acaristan.

AEGIS-Pygame standard: game flow is governed by a strict FSM with
`enter()/exit()/update(dt)/render()` per state, instead of loose string
variables and boolean flags.

This module provides the base classes. The actual State subclasses live in
`acaristan.py` because they need access to module-level state (mouse coords,
menu buttons, save slots, etc.) that's defined there.

Public API:
    GameState           — base class. Override enter/exit/handle_event/update/
                          render/set_ambience.
    GameStateManager    — registry + current state + transition machinery.
                          `transition(name)` is instant; `trigger_transition(name)`
                          does a fade-out → swap → fade-in.

Backward-compat:
    The manager exposes `current_name` and `previous_name` strings so legacy
    code that did `if game_state == "MENU":` can be migrated incrementally to
    `if gsm.current_name == "MENU":` and then fully to FSM dispatch.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pygame


class GameState:
    """Base class for a single game state (MENU, GAME, CUTSCENE, etc.).

    Subclasses override these methods. The default implementations are no-ops
    so a subclass only needs to implement what it cares about.
    """
    name: str = "BASE"

    def enter(self) -> None:
        """Called once when this state becomes active."""
        pass

    def exit(self) -> None:
        """Called once when this state is being left."""
        pass

    def handle_event(self, event: pygame.event.Event,
                     mouse_x: int, mouse_y: int,
                     keys: pygame.key.ScancodeWrapper) -> bool:
        """Handle a single SDL event.

        Returns True if the event was consumed (no further processing).
        Returning False (the default) lets global handlers see it too.
        """
        return False

    def update(self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Advance this state's simulation by `dt` seconds."""
        pass

    def set_ambience(self) -> None:
        """Set audio ambience for this state. Called once per frame."""
        pass

    def render(self, surface: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Draw this state to `surface`."""
        pass


class GameStateManager:
    """Registry + current-state + fade-transition machinery.

    Usage:
        gsm = GameStateManager()
        gsm.add(MenuState())
        gsm.transition("MENU")
        # in main loop:
        gsm.current.handle_event(event, mx, my, keys)
        gsm.current.update(dt)
        gsm.current.render(screen)
        gsm.update_transition()
        gsm.draw_transition(screen)
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.states: dict[str, GameState] = {}
        self.current: GameState | None = None
        self.current_name: str = ""
        self.previous_name: str = ""
        # Fade transition state. `trigger_transition(name)` starts a fade-out;
        # when fade_alpha reaches 255, the manager swaps to the new state and
        # reverses the fade (fade_speed < 0). When fade_alpha returns to 0,
        # transitioning becomes False.
        self.transitioning: bool = False
        self.next_state: str = ""
        self.fade_alpha: int = 0
        self.fade_speed: int = 0
        # Reusable fade surface (lazy-allocated on first draw_transition).
        self._fade_surf: pygame.Surface | None = None

    def add(self, state: GameState) -> None:
        if self.states.get(state.name) is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"State {state.name!r} already registered")
        self.states[state.name] = state

    def transition(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Instant transition: exit current, enter new. No fade."""
        if name not in self.states:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown state {name!r}; registered: {list(self.states)}")
        if self.current is not None:
            self.current.exit()
        self.previous_name = self.current_name
        self.current_name = name
        self.current = self.states[name]
        self.current.enter()

    def trigger_transition(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Faded transition: schedule a fade-out → swap → fade-in.

        Sets `transitioning=True` and `next_state=name`. The main loop must
        call `update_transition()` each frame to advance the fade, and
        `draw_transition(screen)` to blit the fade overlay.
        """
        if name not in self.states:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown state {name!r}; registered: {list(self.states)}")
        self.transitioning = True
        self.next_state = name
        self.fade_speed = 12  # fade-out speed (alpha units per frame)
        # fade_alpha starts at 0 (transparent) and increases toward 255.

    def update_transition(self) -> None:
        """Advance the fade transition. Swaps state at peak alpha.

        Call this every frame regardless of `transitioning` — it's a no-op
        when no transition is in progress.
        """
        if not self.transitioning:
            return
        self.fade_alpha += self.fade_speed
        if self.fade_alpha >= 255:
            # Peak: swap state, reverse fade direction.
            self.fade_alpha = 255
            self.fade_speed = -12  # fade-in speed (negative = alpha decreases)
            # Perform the actual state swap.
            if self.current is not None:
                self.current.exit()
            self.previous_name = self.current_name
            self.current_name = self.next_state
            self.current = self.states[self.next_state]
            self.current.enter()
        elif self.fade_alpha <= 0 and self.fade_speed < 0:
            # Fade-in complete.
            self.fade_alpha = 0
            self.transitioning = False

    def draw_transition(self, surface: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Draw the fade overlay if a transition is in progress."""
        if not self.transitioning:
            return
        if self._fade_surf is None or self._fade_surf.get_size() != surface.get_size():
            self._fade_surf = pygame.Surface(surface.get_size())
        self._fade_surf.fill((0, 0, 0))
        self._fade_surf.set_alpha(min(255, max(0, self.fade_alpha)))
        surface.blit(self._fade_surf, (0, 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# game_draw_unified.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""
game_draw_unified.py — Drop-in replacement for game_core.game_draw()

This module provides the unified game_draw() function that replaces
the mission-routed dispatcher in game_core.py. Instead of:

    def game_draw(fcx, fcy):
        if _is_mission3_active():
            return mission3.game_draw(fcx, fcy)
        if _is_mission2_active():
            return mission2.game_draw(fcx, fcy)
        return mission.game_draw(fcx, fcy)

You now call:

    from game_draw_unified import game_draw
    game_draw(fcx, fcy)

And it routes to the correct GameRenderer population method.

INTEGRATION STEPS:
  1. Copy render_pipeline.py, game_renderer.py, and game_draw_unified.py
     into your game's directory (alongside config.py, state.py, etc.)

  2. In acaristan.py (or wherever game_draw is called), change:
         gc.game_draw(last_fcx, last_fcy)
     to:
         from game_draw_unified import game_draw
         game_draw(last_fcx, last_fcy)

  3. For each mission, fill in the placeholder draw methods in
     game_renderer.py with the actual code from mission.py / mission2.py /
     mission3.py. Each placeholder method has a "Replace with..." comment.

  4. Optionally remove the old mission-specific game_draw() functions
     once all drawing code has been migrated to the renderer.

BENEFITS:
  - Adding a new visual layer = adding one pipeline.submit() call
  - Y-sorting entities is automatic (sort_key=rect.centery)
  - Post-processing is always last, always consistent
  - No more duplicated draw code between missions
  - New missions just add a populate_mN() method
"""


def game_draw(fcx, fcy):
    """Unified game draw entry point.

    Routes to the correct GameRenderer population method based on
    the active mission, then flushes the pipeline.
    """
    from game_renderer import GameRenderer
    import game_core as gc

    active = getattr(gc, "active_mission", "MISSION1")

    renderer = GameRenderer(fcx, fcy, snap_camera=True)

    if active == "MISSION3":
        renderer.populate_m3()
    elif active == "MISSION2":
        renderer.populate_m2()
    else:
        renderer.populate_m1()

    renderer.flush()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# game_renderer.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""
game_renderer.py — Unified game drawing for all three missions.

Replaces the 3 separate game_draw() functions in mission.py, mission2.py,
and mission3.py with a single pipeline-driven renderer.

ARCHITECTURE:
  1. Each mission registers "draw submissions" into the RenderPipeline
     at the correct layer.
  2. Mission-specific elements are registered by the mission's own
     `populate_pipeline()` method.
  3. The shared skeleton (bullets, player, particles, HUD, post-FX)
     is drawn by this module — missions don't duplicate it.
  4. `flush()` draws everything in layer order with Y-sorting.

MIGRATION PATH:
  - mission.py: replace game_draw() body with:
        renderer = GameRenderer(fcx, fcy)
        renderer.populate_m1()
        renderer.flush()
  - mission2.py: replace game_draw() body with:
        renderer = GameRenderer(fcx, fcy)
        renderer.populate_m2()
        renderer.flush()
  - mission3.py: replace game_draw() body with:
        renderer = GameRenderer(fcx, fcy)
        renderer.populate_m3()
        renderer.flush()
"""

import math
import pygame
from render_pipeline import RenderPipeline
from config import (
    WIDTH, HEIGHT, TILE_SIZE, screen, C_BG_GAME,
    font_terminal_small, C_RAIN, C_BULLET, bullet_glow, MUZZLE_FLASH,
    draw_scanlines, draw_vignette,
)
from art_cache import get_blood_decal, get_glow, get_fullscreen_overlay
from state import STATE
from user_settings import SETTINGS
from camera import draw_bullets


class GameRenderer:
    """Unified game renderer using the RenderPipeline.

    Attributes:
        fcx, fcy: Raw camera floats (from update_camera).
        cam_x, cam_y: Integer-snapped camera (prevents tile shimmer).
        pipeline: The RenderPipeline instance for this frame.
    """

    def __init__(self, fcx, fcy, snap_camera=True):
        self.fcx = fcx
        self.fcy = fcy
        # Integer-snapped camera prevents tile/prop seam shimmer when
        # the camera scrolls by fractional pixels. M1 used raw floats;
        # M2/M3 snapped. We snap by default for consistency.
        if snap_camera:
            self.cam_x = int(round(fcx))
            self.cam_y = int(round(fcy))
        else:
            self.cam_x = fcx
            self.cam_y = fcy
        self.pipeline = RenderPipeline()

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────
    # SHARED SKELETON SUBMISSIONS
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────

    def _submit_shared_world(self):
        """Submit draw calls shared by all missions: bullets, thrown bottles,
        enemies, player, particles, casings, pickups, floating texts."""

        cam_x, cam_y = self.cam_x, self.cam_y

        # ── Bullets (shared helper from camera.py) ──
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'projectiles',
            lambda s: draw_bullets(s, STATE.bullets, cam_x, cam_y, with_glow=True),
        )

        # ── Thrown bottles ──
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'projectiles',
            lambda s: self._draw_thrown_bottles(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            sort_key=0,
        )

        # ── Enemies (Y-sorted by centery) ──
        for e in STATE.enemies:
            sort_key = e.rect.centery
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'entities',
                lambda s, _e=e: _e.draw(s, cam_x, cam_y),
                sort_key=sort_key,
            )

        # ── Player ──
        if STATE.player:
            import death_anim
            if not death_anim.should_skip_player_draw():
                reload_max_p = 90 if getattr(STATE, "current_weapon", "pistol") == "os12" else 60
                reload_progress = (1.0 - STATE.reload_timer / reload_max_p
                                   if STATE.is_reloading and STATE.reload_timer > 0 else 0.0)
                melee_progress = (1.0 - STATE.melee_timer / 18.0
                                  if STATE.melee_active and STATE.melee_timer > 0 else 0.0)
                # Import the module-level _last_keys from whichever mission is active.
                # Each mission module defines its own; we read it from game_core proxy.
                import game_core as gc
                last_keys = getattr(gc, '_last_keys', None)
                is_moving = (not STATE.player_dead and last_keys and (
                    last_keys[pygame.K_w] or last_keys[pygame.K_s] or
                    last_keys[pygame.K_a] or last_keys[pygame.K_d]
                ))
                self.pipeline.submit(
                    'entities',
                    lambda s: STATE.player.draw(
                        s, cam_x, cam_y, STATE.walls,
                        STATE.is_reloading, reload_progress,
                        STATE.melee_active, melee_progress,
                        is_moving=is_moving,
                    ),
                    sort_key=STATE.player.rect.centery,
                )

        # ── Particles ──
        for p in STATE.particles:
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'effects',
                lambda s, _p=p: _p.draw(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # ── Casings ──
        for c in STATE.casings:
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'effects',
                lambda s, _c=c: _c.draw(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # ── Pickups ──
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'items',
            lambda s: self._draw_pickups(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # ── Floating texts ──
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'floating',
            lambda s: self._draw_floating_texts(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

    def _submit_shared_overlays(self):
        """Submit overlay draw calls shared by all missions:
        muzzle flash, death overlay, flash overlay, post-FX, HUD."""

        cam_x, cam_y = self.cam_x, self.cam_y

        # ── Muzzle flash ──
        if STATE.muzzle_flash_timer > 0 and STATE.player:
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'overlay',
                lambda s: self._draw_muzzle_flash(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # ── Death overlay ──
        if STATE.player_dead:
            import death_anim
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'overlay',
                lambda s: death_anim.draw_death_overlay(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # ── GC flash overlay (grenade/blast white flash) ──
        if STATE.gc_flash_timer > 0 and not getattr(STATE, "reduced_motion", False):
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'overlay',
                lambda s: self._draw_gc_flash(s),
            )

        # ── Post-processing (scanlines + vignette) ──
        # Vignette strength varies by mission — set via self.vignette_strength
        vignette_strength = getattr(self, 'vignette_strength', 130)
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'postprocess',
            lambda s: draw_vignette(s, strength=vignette_strength),
        )
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'postprocess',
            lambda s: draw_scanlines(s),
        )

        # ── HUD (drawn after post-FX so it sits on top) ──
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'hud',
            lambda s: self._draw_hud(s),
        )

        # ── Camera tilt (death) — drawn absolutely last ──
        if STATE.player_dead:
            import death_anim
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'hud',
                lambda s: death_anim.apply_camera_tilt(s),
            )

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────
    # SHARED DRAW HELPERS
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _draw_thrown_bottles(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """Draw molotov bottles in flight."""
        for b in STATE.thrown_bottles:
            t = b["t"]
            bx = b["x"] - cam_x
            by = b["y"] - cam_y - math.sin(t * math.pi) * 40
            # Flame
            pygame.draw.circle(surface, (255, 120, 35), (int(bx), int(by)), 5)
            # Bottle neck
            pygame.draw.line(surface, (90, 55, 25), (bx, by), (bx + 3, by - 12), 3)

    @staticmethod
    def _draw_pickups(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """Draw pickup items. Missions can override by not calling this."""
        for pu in STATE.pickups:
            px = pu["x"] - cam_x
            py = pu["y"] - cam_y
            if -50 < px < WIDTH + 50 and -50 < py < HEIGHT + 50:
                # Generic pickup glow + rect
                glow = get_glow(14, (200, 200, 100), 40)
                surface.blit(glow, (px - 14, py - 14))
                rect = pygame.Rect(px - 10, py - 10, 20, 20)
                pygame.draw.rect(surface, (40, 40, 38), rect)
                pygame.draw.rect(surface, (100, 95, 80), rect, 1)

    @staticmethod
    def _draw_floating_texts(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """Draw floating text popups."""
        pinned = [ft for ft in STATE.floating_texts if len(ft) >= 6 and ft[5] == "pin"]
        unpinned = [ft for ft in STATE.floating_texts if not (len(ft) >= 6 and ft[5] == "pin")]
        for ft in unpinned:
            txt = font_terminal_small.render(ft[2], True, ft[3])
            surface.blit(txt, (ft[0] - cam_x - txt.get_width() // 2, ft[1] - cam_y))

    @staticmethod
    def _draw_muzzle_flash(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """Draw the player's muzzle flash at barrel tip."""
        if STATE.player:
            tip_x, tip_y = STATE.player.barrel_tip()
            surface.blit(
                MUZZLE_FLASH,
                (int(tip_x - cam_x - 40), int(tip_y - cam_y - 40)),
            )
            STATE.muzzle_flash_timer -= 1

    @staticmethod
    def _draw_gc_flash(surface):
        """Draw the grenade/blast white flash overlay."""
        flash_surf = get_fullscreen_overlay((255, 255, 255, 255))
        flash_surf.set_alpha(min(255, STATE.gc_flash_timer * 22))
        surface.blit(flash_surf, (0, 0))

    def _draw_hud(self, surface):
        """Draw the HUD. Overridden per-mission via self.hud_drawer."""
        hud_drawer = getattr(self, 'hud_drawer', None)
        if hud_drawer:
            hud_drawer(surface)

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────
    # MISSION 1 POPULATION
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────

    def populate_m1(self):
        """Populate the pipeline with Mission 1 (Black Notebook) draws."""
        cam_x, cam_y = self.cam_x, self.cam_y
        self.vignette_strength = 130

        # Background fill
        self.pipeline.submit('floor', lambda s: s.fill(C_BG_GAME))

        # Floor tiles — M1 specific (warehouse vs slum tiles)
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'floor',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_floors(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Walls + shadows — M1 specific (warehouse walls vs containers)
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'walls',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_walls(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Breach markers
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'doors',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_breach_markers(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Desks
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'items',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_desks(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Doors (bay doors + regular doors)
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'doors',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_doors(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Blood decals
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'decals',
            lambda s: self._draw_blood_decals(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Fire zones
        for fz in STATE.fire_zones:
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'effects',
                lambda s, _fz=fz: _fz.draw(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # Shared world elements (bullets, enemies, player, particles, etc.)
        self._submit_shared_world()

        # M1-specific entities drawn between shared layers
        # Volkov / Commander escape NPCs
        if getattr(STATE, 'firefight_triggered', False) and getattr(STATE, 'volkov_escape_timer', 0) > 0:
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'entities',
                lambda s: self._m1_draw_escape_npcs(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # Notebook glow + prompt
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'hud',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_notebook_prompt(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Exfil truck
        self.pipeline.submit(
            'hud',
            lambda s: self._m1_draw_exfil_truck(s, cam_x, cam_y),
        )

        # Hotwire overlay (drawn on top of gameplay but below HUD)
        if getattr(STATE, 'truck_hotwiring', False):
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'overlay',
                lambda s: self._m1_draw_hotwire(s, cam_x, cam_y),
            )

        # Breach flicker
        if getattr(STATE, 'breach_stage', 0) in (3, 4):
            self.pipeline.submit(
                'overlay',
                lambda s: self._m1_draw_breach_flicker(s),
            )

        # Set HUD drawer for M1
        self.hud_drawer = self._m1_draw_hud

        # Shared overlays (post-FX, death, etc.)
        self._submit_shared_overlays()

    # ── M1-specific draw helpers ──

    @staticmethod
    def _m1_draw_floors(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """M1 floor tiles: warehouse tiles vs slum tiles."""
        from config import FLOOR_TILE_SIZE, FLOOR_TILE, SLUM_FLOOR_TILE
        start_tx = int(cam_x // FLOOR_TILE_SIZE) * FLOOR_TILE_SIZE
        start_ty = int(cam_y // FLOOR_TILE_SIZE) * FLOOR_TILE_SIZE
        warehouse_y_start = 11 * TILE_SIZE
        warehouse_y_end = 20 * TILE_SIZE
        for tx in range(
            start_tx - FLOOR_TILE_SIZE,
            int(cam_x + WIDTH + FLOOR_TILE_SIZE * 2),
            FLOOR_TILE_SIZE,
        ):
            for ty in range(
                start_ty - FLOOR_TILE_SIZE,
                int(cam_y + HEIGHT + FLOOR_TILE_SIZE * 2),
                FLOOR_TILE_SIZE,
            ):
                tile = (
                    FLOOR_TILE
                    if (warehouse_y_start <= ty <= warehouse_y_end)
                    else SLUM_FLOOR_TILE
                )
                surface.blit(tile, (tx - cam_x, ty - cam_y))

    @staticmethod
    def _m1_draw_walls(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """M1 walls: warehouse walls vs colored container tiles."""
        from config import WAREHOUSE_WALL
        container_tiles = []  # Will be populated from config
        try:
            from config import (CONTAINER_TILE_RED, CONTAINER_TILE_BLUE,
                                CONTAINER_TILE_RUST, CONTAINER_TILE_GREY, wall_shadow)
            container_tiles = [CONTAINER_TILE_RED, CONTAINER_TILE_BLUE,
                               CONTAINER_TILE_RUST, CONTAINER_TILE_GREY]
        except ImportError:
            pass
        for wall in STATE.walls:
            dr = pygame.Rect(wall.x - cam_x, wall.y - cam_y, TILE_SIZE, TILE_SIZE)
            try:
                surface.blit(wall_shadow, (dr.x - 4, dr.y - 4))
            except NameError:
                pass
            col = wall.x // TILE_SIZE
            row = wall.y // TILE_SIZE
            if (col, row) in getattr(STATE, 'warehouse_walls_set', set()):
                surface.blit(WAREHOUSE_WALL, (dr.x, dr.y))
            elif container_tiles:
                tile_idx = (col + row) % len(container_tiles)
                surface.blit(container_tiles[tile_idx], (dr.x, dr.y))

    @staticmethod
    def _m1_draw_breach_markers(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """M1 breach markers: pulsing orange circles on breachable walls."""
        for marker in STATE.breach_markers[:]:
            mx, my, timer = marker
            mx -= cam_x
            my -= cam_y
            if -50 < mx < WIDTH + 50 and -50 < my < HEIGHT + 50:
                alpha = min(255, timer * 2)
                for i in range(3):
                    radius = 8 + i * 4
                    s = get_glow(radius, (255, 80, 20), 255)
                    s.set_alpha(alpha // (i + 1))
                    surface.blit(s, (mx - radius, my - radius))
            marker[2] -= 1
            if marker[2] <= 0:
                STATE.breach_markers.remove(marker)

    @staticmethod
    def _m1_draw_desks(surface, cam_x, cam_y):
        """M1 desks with papers, notes, coffee mugs, and read indicators.
        NOTE: The full desk drawing is ~30 lines of detailed pygame.draw calls.
        This is a simplified placeholder — replace with the original code
        from mission.py when integrating."""
        for desk in STATE.desks:
            dx = desk["x"] - cam_x
            dy = desk["y"] - cam_y
            if -50 < dx < WIDTH + 50 and -50 < dy < HEIGHT + 50:
                # Desk body
                pygame.draw.rect(surface, (62, 50, 38), (dx - 24, dy - 16, 48, 32))
                pygame.draw.rect(surface, (80, 65, 48), (dx - 24, dy - 16, 48, 32), 1)
                # Read indicator
                dot_col = (100, 220, 100) if desk.get("read") else (240, 190, 50)
                pygame.draw.circle(surface, dot_col, (dx, dy - 22), 4)
